title: Jason and the Golden Fleece
subtitle: The quest of the Argonauts
subject: mythologie
description: Jason and the Argonauts sail to Colchis to bring back the Golden Fleece. Behind the adventure lies a story of love and betrayal with the sorceress Medea.

hero.hook: Fifty heroes, a magic ship, a fleece guarded by a dragon. And a sorceress without whom none of it would have worked.

blocks.text: **Jason** gathers the **[[Argonauts]]**, an elite band of Greek heroes, to go and fetch the **Golden Fleece**: the hide of a divine ram, hung up in [[Colchis]], a region that roughly matches present-day Georgia.

This voyage is one of the oldest sea stories in the West. It is about royal legitimacy, divine help, and above all the destructive passion between Jason and **Medea**, the sorceress who makes the victory possible and then terrible.

sections.title: A sandal, a throne, a trap

blocks.text: Jason is the son of Aeson, king of Iolcos in Thessaly. His uncle [[Pelias]] has seized the throne. Raised by the centaur [[Chiron]], Jason comes back to claim his inheritance. On the way he helps an old woman across a torrent. She is [[Hera]] in disguise. He loses one sandal in the mud.
In Colchis, sheepskins were sometimes laid on riverbeds to trap flakes of gold. The “golden fleece” may have a real mining origin.

Pelias is afraid: an oracle had warned him about the man with a single sandal. He promises the throne if Jason brings back the Fleece, which a dragon guards. Jason has the [[Argo]] built, a ship whose prow can speak thanks to sacred wood from [[Dodona]]. On board: **Heracles**, **Orpheus**, **Castor and Pollux**, and many others.

blocks.caption: The Argo, the first great ship of Greek legend

blocks.text: On the way, the Argonauts save King Phineus from the **Harpies**, monsters that kept stealing his food. In return, Phineus tells them how to pass the **Symplegades**, cliffs that crush any ship entering the Black Sea.

Jason releases a dove. The rocks close on its tail feathers, then open again. The Argo slips through. In Colchis, King **Aeetes** sets impossible tasks: yoke bulls that breathe fire, plow the field of [[Ares]], sow dragon's teeth that grow into warriors. Without help, Jason would die.

[[Aphrodite]], goddess of love, makes **Medea** fall for Jason. Medea is the daughter of Aeetes and a priestess of [[Hecate]]. She gives him an ointment against the fire of the bulls. For the warriors born from the teeth, she tells him to throw a stone into the middle of them: they kill each other.

blocks.caption: Medea and Jason: magic in the service of the quest

blocks.text: At last she puts the dragon to sleep. Jason takes down the Fleece. To escape, Medea kills her brother **Apsyrtus** and scatters his remains at sea. Aeetes stops to gather the body. The couple is united, and already cursed.

In Iolcos, Pelias refuses to step down. Medea tricks his daughters: they “rejuvenate” their father by cutting him to pieces. Driven out, the couple takes refuge in Corinth. Years later, Jason wants to marry the daughter of King Creon. Medea takes her revenge: a poisoned dress for her rival, then the murder of their own children.

Jason grows old alone. He dies wretchedly, crushed by a rotten beam of the Argo as he rests beneath it. The hero who won everything through the help of others is destroyed for disowning the woman who saved him.
Jason wins the Fleece thanks to Medea and the [[Argo]]. His betrayal breaks their pact and leads to ruin: the myth shows that a hero who disowns his allies ends up losing everything.
